Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:14:12 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sudden 5xx burst + timeouts hitting our production traffic

Hey Vivek / Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and connection timeouts from Redwood around 09:10 PDT. Error rates jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% in ~3 minutes; retries at our edge caused a noticeable client-side slowdown. Attached is a quick dashboard snapshot (acme-5xx-graphs.png).

Context: we are in a peak billing batch window (heavy embeddings + long conversational prompts). Traffic is routed to your Dedicated pool for our enterprise account (ACME-ENT-2026). We haven’t changed client timeouts or retry config.

Asks: can we get an immediate status update and join an emergency bridge? We’re seeing latency tail increases and several upstream client retries causing request amplification.

— Samantha
Samantha Cho
Head of Platform Ops, AcmeCloud
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@acmecloud.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:22:35 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden 5xx burst + timeouts hitting our production traffic

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the heads-up and the dashboard. We’re bringing the infra on-call and SREs into the bridge now. Preliminary triage: our telemetry shows a short-lived GPU queue stall in your Dedicated pool coincident with autoscaler provisioning delays; that can produce 5xx spikes and client-side timeouts, especially for long-sequence runs.

Immediate steps we’re taking (ETA ~30m):
- Open emergency bridge (link shared in separate chat).
- Temporarily enable fallback routing to your warm-host fallback pool (shorter sequence/quantized variant).
- Increase autoscaler aggressiveness on the Dedicated pool by one step to absorb burst.
- Ask you to lower client-side retry backoff for the next 15 minutes if possible (we’ll confirm when stable).

Can your team join the bridge? We’ll also collect heap dump and kernel-level logs and share them.

Vivek
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:03:08 -07:00
Subject: AcmeCloud 5xx — quick debug notes and mitigations applied

Team — summary of what I’m seeing from the runtime side after joining the bridge: 

- Observed symptoms: sudden queue-depth spike on pool acme-dedicated-us-west; autoscaler requested new nodes at 09:11:02 but instance spin-up lagged ~90–120s due to a cloud-prov saturation in the region. During that lag we saw kernel OOM/rejects surface as 502/504s at the front door.
- Root-candidate: capacity exhaustion + autoscale lag + client retry amplification for long-context models. Not a model crash.

Mitigations executed (10:00–10:20 PDT):
- Force-provisioned an extra warm node from the dedicated pool spare quota (applied at 09:23).
- Flipped routing to fallback-quantized-1 (lower-memory variant) for requests with seq_len > 1024.
- Deployed short-term rate-limiter on inbound edge to damp client retry loops for 5 min windows.
- Grabbed heapdump (heapdump-20270522.log) and kernel traces uploaded to the incident drive.

Next steps (owners):
- SRE (lauren): dig into cloud provider allocation logs and confirm why spin-up delayed beyond normal SLOs.
- Runtime (hannah): reproduce queue stall locally with a synthetic long-seq traffic generator; validate preemption behavior.
- Eng Ops (vivek): align on formal customer message and postmortem timeline.

Note: we also recommended a client-side retry policy change to Acme so they don’t amplify the burst.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary for leadership — AcmeCloud 5xx spike (for follow-up)

Hi all — forwarding a short exec-friendly summary to attach to the account brief and to escalate pricing/credits discussion later: 

On May 22, ~09:10 PDT Acme experienced a sudden increase in 5xx rates driven by a short period (~2–3 minutes) where Dedicated pool capacity hit a hard envelope while autoscaler latency prevented immediate node replacement. Client retries amplified the problem and produced a transient retry storm. We applied fallback routing and forced provisioning; error rates returned to baseline by ~09:45.

Impact: customer-facing errors and increased tail latency during a high-value billing window. Potential commercial implications if we cannot demonstrate mitigating actions and a P1 postmortem.

Immediate asks for leadership:
- Approve a goodwill credit proposal (tbd amount) and a dedicated postmortem with Acme within 72 hours.
- Approve an ops follow-up to increase Dedicated pool warm-reserve for large enterprise accounts in us-west.

Subject: Status update: AcmeCloud 5xx burst — mitigations in place and next steps

Samantha / Acme Ops team —

Thank you for the quick signal and for joining the bridge earlier. Short update and concrete next steps: 

What happened (short): a transient capacity exhaustion in your Dedicated pool combined with autoscaler spin-up lag produced a brief window of 5xx errors and timeouts; client retries magnified the effect.

What we did: 
- Forced an extra warm node into your Dedicated pool and enabled fallback routing to a quantized variant for large sequences.
- Deployed a temporary edge retry-dampening rule (5 min) to prevent amplification.
- Collected heap and kernel traces (attached).

Status now: error rate returned to baseline (~0.25%) and tail latency improved. We will keep the fallback route for one more hour while we validate full capacity.

Follow-ups: 
- We will run a formal postmortem (owners: Marissa + Hannah) and share findings within 72 hours (JIRA: JIRA-INC-5543).
- Proposal: increase your warm-reserve for the Dedicated pool by X units during high-volume windows; I’ll follow up with account team on timing and cost.
- Can you confirm if we should proceed with a scheduled model migration to quantized-variant later tonight (low-traffic window)? That will reduce per-token memory pressure but requires a brief config flip.

Attachments: playbook-delta.pdf, heapdump-20270522.log

We appreciate the quick collaboration. Please ping me directly if you see any recurrence.

— Vivek
VP, Product Operations
